proof_summary: Take \(n=716{,}993{,}899\), so \(2n-1=1{,}433{,}987{,}797\); size bounds force any possible exponents to lie between \(1\) and \(30\). An exhaustive check of these exponent pairs shows that every residual \(1{,}433{,}987{,}797-2^x-7\cdot2^y\) is either ineligible by size, composite, or not congruent to \(5\pmod 6\), so this unlisted \(n\) has value zero.
